result.title: Old Is Not False: Valid-Time Memory for Interactive Video World Models
result.summary: Interactive video world models draw each frame from a memory bank of earlier frames stamped with their capture times. With frames, weights and noise fixed, reversing the timestamps of two views flips the state that generators of two families draw: they take the newest timestamp as the truth. That reading is right as long as states never return. After an agent undoes an action, the newest view of a region is outdated and the only view of the present is older; memories for changing worlds delete that older view, and memories that keep it hand the generator the past. Temporal databases separate when a record is stored from when its content holds, its valid time. ReDate keeps every frame and dates each retrieved token by its valid time, read from the agent's action log. The frozen generator then reads a reverted region as one that has just reached a new state, so ReDate needs no training. We prove that trusting the newest timestamp is right exactly when every current view is dated after every outdated one, that without a view taken after the return only the action log tells a reverted region from an up-to-date one, and that a generator able to draw from its own prediction gains more from re-dating than from deletion when the moved tokens keep little weight. After an undo, ReDate raises the share of FAR's steps showing the current state from 0.36 to 0.62 and HY-WorldPlay's from 0.003 to 0.19. We also propose a calibrated state metric to test any memory after undos.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ReDate，为交互式视频世界模型的记忆帧引入「有效时间」：由智能体动作日志为每个检索到的 token 标注其内容真正成立的时间，使冻结生成器在动作回退后无需训练即可把已回退区域读成刚到达的新状态；并给出「信任最新时间戳」何时成立的理论分析和一个校准的状态度量。
AI.relevance_reason: 对检索记忆中「过期证据与当前证据」的区分、以及免训练地对缓存 token 重新标注，可能为 LVR 中检索到的视觉证据时效性、缓存结构与状态回退处理提供可核查的方法线索；但对象是视频世界模型而非多模态推理本身。
